record.original_question: Let G be a finitely-generated Fuchsian group of the first kind. (a) If F : Π → Π is a G-invariant quasi-symmetric function, is F totally singular? (b) Is the Teichmuller space TG dense in the space SG (Schwarzians of G-invariant univalent functions)? (O. Lehto; L. Bers; I. Kra; communicated by D. Hamilton)

evidence.quote: Let G be a finitely-generated Fuchsian group of the first kind. (a) If F : Π → Π is a G-invariant quasi-symmetric function, is F totally singular?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Pi$ denote the upper half-plane in $\mathbb{C}$, and let $G$ be a finitely-generated Fuchsian group of the first kind acting on $\Pi$ (i.e., a discrete subgroup of $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ whose limit set on $\partial\Pi=\mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ is all of $\partial\Pi$, and which has a finite-sided fundamental domain). 

A homeomorphism $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is called quasi-symmetric if there is a constant $M\geq 1$ such that $\frac{1}{M}\leq \frac{f(x+t)-f(x)}{f(x)-f(x-t)}\leq M$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$ and $t>0$. By the Beurling–Ahlfors extension, such $f$ extends to a quasiconformal homeomorphism $F:\Pi\to\Pi$. Call $F$ $G$-invariant if for every $g\in G$ there exists a Möbius transformation $g'$ preserving $\Pi$ with $F\circ g = g'\circ F$. Call $F$ totally singular if its boundary values $f$ map a set of full measure on $\mathbb{R}$ onto a set of measure zero (equivalently, $f$ is singular as a function).

Let $S_G$ denote the space of Schwarzian derivatives $S_h$ of all univalent meromorphic functions $h$ on the lower half-plane $\Pi^*$ that are $G$-compatible (i.e., for each $g\in G$ there is a Möbius transformation $g'$ with $h\circ g = g'\circ h$ on $\Pi^*$), regarded as a subset of the Banach space of bounded holomorphic quadratic differentials for $G$ on $\Pi^*$. Let $T_G\subset S_G$ denote the Teichmüller space of $G$, consisting of those Schwarzians $S_h$ where $h$ admits a quasiconformal extension to $\mathbb{C}$.

Answer the following:

(a) Is every $G$-invariant quasi-symmetric homeomorphism $F:\Pi\to\Pi$ totally singular?

(b) Is $T_G$ dense in $S_G$?
artifact.status_search_result: A focused web search did not return any source explicitly resolving either part of the question for finitely-generated Fuchsian groups of the first kind. Standard references on Bers embeddings, Schwarzian parametrizations, and Teichmüller spaces of Fuchsian groups appear, but none were found that directly settle (a) total singularity of G-invariant quasi-symmetric maps or (b) density of T_G in S_G. Status is therefore recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.snippet: Studies of Teichmüller spaces inside the space of Schwarzians for finitely-generated Fuchsian groups.
status_evidence.claim: Background on T_G as a subset of the Schwarzian space, but does not directly settle the density question.

status_evidence.title: Teichmüller space - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Bers embedding realizes the Teichmüller space of a Fuchsian group G as an open bounded contractible subset of the Banach space of bounded quadratic differentials.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms framework for T_G ⊂ S_G but no statement about density.
